name: Stylage

lead: Stylage is a range of cross-linked hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers made by the French company Laboratoires Vivacy. Its distinguishing feature is mannitol in the gel, added as an antioxidant. Products are used for fine lines, nasolabial folds, lip augmentation and facial volume.

In practice, a clinician injects the gel to restore volume or add definition, for example to a lip or a fold. Randomised trials of Stylage products against other HA fillers have reported non-inferior results on wrinkle and lip outcomes.

paras: Treatment is done by a trained injector who chooses a product from the range based on the area and the softness needed. Results are visible immediately and HA fillers typically last months before being absorbed. Many products include lidocaine to reduce injection discomfort.

Common effects are swelling, redness, bruising and tenderness. Less common complications include lumps and infection, and rare vascular events can cause tissue damage. Fillers are regulated as medical devices, and the number of products cleared varies by country.

angle.text: Stylage gels are placed where volume is wanted, such as the lips or nasolabial folds, and the change is visible immediately and fades as the gel is absorbed.

lead: Stylage is a range of hyaluronic acid dermal fillers from Laboratoires Vivacy, a French manufacturer. Its gels are cross-linked HA containing mannitol, and the range includes products for superficial lines, deeper folds, lips and volume [1].

People use HA fillers to change how the face looks: smoothing nasolabial folds, adding lip volume or definition, and restoring lost volume. Reviews describe injectable HA fillers as minimally invasive procedures that replace lost volume and soften grooves for a more youthful appearance [1].

Published trials have compared Stylage products with established fillers. A randomised study in Chinese adults found Stylage L non-inferior to Restylane for nasolabial folds at six months [2], and a split-face trial found Stylage L Lidocaine non-inferior to Juvederm Ultra 3 [3].

paras: A 2013 review describes Stylage as a product line whose manufacture includes mannitol, and discusses its physicochemical properties [1]. Most HA fillers are cross-linked with BDDE for stability [4], and studies compare how different crosslinking technologies change HA behaviour [5].

A multicentre, quadruple-blind randomised trial compared four HA fillers for lip augmentation [6]. A separate non-inferiority study of a Vivacy lip product with lidocaine reported that the difference in improved subjects between arms was +7.0 percentage points (90 percent CI -2.2 to 17.7) against a margin of -15, meeting the non-inferiority criterion [7]. A retrospective study of 30 patients described a technique using two Stylage products with different injection planes [8].

In the NICE study, 47 of 50 randomised subjects were analysed, and Stylage L Lidocaine was non-inferior to Juvederm Ultra 3 on the Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale at six months [3]. In a 390-person Chinese study, Stylage L met non-inferiority against Restylane, with wrinkle responder rates statistically higher in the Stylage group at six months [2].

Randomised comparative trials exist for nasolabial folds [2][3] and lips [6][7]. The trials were non-inferiority designs against established HA fillers. A preliminary report examined cross-linked HA for cleft lip and palate aesthetic correction [9].

Dermal filler reference pages list bruising, redness, pain and itching as common effects, with infection, lumps and delayed reactions less common, and blindness from retrograde embolisation and skin necrosis as rare serious events [4]. Fillers are regulated as medical devices: only six were approved in the US, versus over 140 on the UK and EU market, according to Wikipedia [4].
